steps.title: Prepare HEK293T cells for assay
steps.instruction: Rinse, detach, collect, and plate HEK293T cells to obtain enough confluent cells for one UFMylation sample.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate the culture medium and add 5–10 mL sterile PBS to rinse the cells.
Aspirate the PBS and add 1 mL Trypsin‑EDTA solution A (0.25%) to detach cells; incubate in the cell incubator at 37 °C.
Add 5 mL complete DMEM, resuspend the cells, and transfer the suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 150 × g for 3 min, then carefully aspirate the supernatant with a vacuum pump.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 40 mL complete DMEM and divide evenly into four 10‑cm diameter plates (one 10‑cm dish at 90–100 % confluence provides sufficient cells for one sample).

steps.title: Produce recombinant UFL1 and DDRGK1 proteins
steps.instruction: Express, purify, and store GST‑tagged DDRGK1 or UFL1 from BL21 (DE3) E. coli using IPTG induction and GST‑Sepharose chromatography.

substeps.instruction: Culture BL21 (DE3) E. coli harboring pGEX‑6P‑1‑DDRGK1 or pGEX‑6P‑1‑UFL1 in 1 L LB at 37 °C for 3–5 h with shaking at 220 rpm until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.6.
Add 5 mL IPTG (100 mM) to achieve a final IPTG concentration of 0.5 mM; continue shaking at 19 °C for 16–18 h.
Transfer the culture to 200 mL centrifuge tubes and spin at 8,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 50 mL pre‑cold PBS containing 1× protease inhibitor cocktail (Roche) and 1 mM PMSF.
Lyse the cells with a high‑pressure cell disrupter for 2–3 cycles.
Centrifuge the crude lysate at 14,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Equilibrate a 1 mL GST‑Sepharose gravity column with 5 mL (5 CV) pre‑cold 1× PBS containing 0.5 % Triton X‑100 (PBS‑X).
Load approximately 50 mL of the cleared supernatant onto the column.
Wash the column with 15 CV of PBS‑X.
Drain the column by gravity and incubate it with 1 mL PBS‑X containing PreScission Protease at 4 °C for 16 h.
Collect the flow‑through, add glycerol to a final concentration of 20 %, aliquot, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 1 mg/mL PEI transfection solution
steps.instruction: Make a sterile 1 mg/mL polyethyleneimine solution (pH 7.0) suitable for HEK293T transfection and store at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Measure ~450 mL distilled, sterilized water into a 500 mL glass beaker.
Dissolve 500 mg PEI in the water while stirring.
Add ~1 mL concentrated HCl (12 M) dropwise to lower the pH below 2.0.
Stir for 2–3 h until the PEI is fully dissolved.
Add 1–2 mL NaOH (3 M) dropwise to raise the pH to 7.0.
Transfer the solution to a 500 mL glass cylinder and adjust the final volume to 500 mL with the remaining water.
Sterile‑filter the solution through a 0.22 µm membrane using a sterile 20 mL syringe.
Aliquot the PEI solution into 1 mL or 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and store at –20 °C.

description: Preparing high quality plasmid DNAs and HEK293T cells for UFMylation assay in cells, and preparing recombinant proteins of each UFMylation components for UFMylation assay in vitro. This protocol describes a detailed procedure for UFMylation analysis in cells and in vitro assay. UFMylation is a recently identified ubiquitin-like modification, which covalently conjugates the ubiquitin-like protein UFM1 to target proteins through a three-step enzymatic cascade catalyzed sequentially by UFM1-activating enzyme 5 (UBA5, E1), UFM1-conjugating enzyme 1 (UFC1, E2), UFM1-specific ligase 1 (UFL1, E3) and cofactor DDRGK1 (Komatsu et al., 2004; Gerakis et al., 2019). For UFMylation assay in human cells, we transiently transfect the expression plasmids of UFMylation component (E1, E2, E3, DDRGK1 and UFM1) and the Flag-tagged substrate protein (FLAG-p53) into HEK293T cells, followed by immunoprecipitation with Flag beads and immunoblotting to detect the UFMylated protein with the UFM1 antibody. For in vitro UFMylation assay, we reconstitute UFMylation reaction system with the purified UFMylation components in vitro, followed by immunoblotting to detect the UFMylated protein.
